doc.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021

title: Playing for Liza Minnelli in 1979
summary: He got the Liza Minnelli gig as a late call on Lawrence Feldman's recommendation, and handles keys and her spontaneity.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: You know. When I got the gig with Liza Minelli for a while, which is 1979, which I was definitely the 15th call or something because they had asked Lawrence Feldman my friend. They got to the saxophones to ask about piano players. And so Lawrence Feldman recommended me. So you know when a saxophone player is recommending you that they’ve gone down the list of people. But all these guys were studio guys in New York and didn’t want to travel. So I got a chance to do that, get very well paid for a little while, and see some show business.
Did you have to be ready to play songs that you knew in different keys with Liza or with female singers?

Sure. Absolutely yeah that was part of the fun for me. At the beginning I was not a very good transposer. You know if I knew that I had to do it I would write out a quick lead sheet or at least the chords in other keys. But then it got to be where most of the tunes I knew well enough, especially if there was a chart I mean it was not a problem. But I remember one night with Liza there was an intro, I gave her a D7 and we used to just — because she could be very spontaneous and funny. But the show was very scripted. It was the same every night. When something would happen, like when part of the stage would fall down and she’d ad lib, we’d just love it. So, and she was very cool that way, she was really very cool. And then one night I gave her the D7 which was supposed to go to “Someone to Watch Over Me” or something, I think in G. So I gave her whatever the chord was, and she went into another tune in G. And I was right there.
